instruction: Extract helloExtension.zip on the Desktop to the Desktop and then import the unpacked extension into Chrome.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Variation with direct imperative instruction style. Task requires extracting the extension archive and loading it into Chrome as an unpacked extension. Uses standard Chrome evaluator pattern: get_find_unpacked_extension_path queries Chrome preferences for all loaded extensions, is_in_list validates the expected path appears in the results.
metadata.verification: Verified evaluator logic: Chrome Preferences file in .config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences contains extension settings with path field, getter extracts all paths, metric checks list membership.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both extraction and loading requirements by checking Chrome Preferences file for unpacked extension path
Getter function get_find_unpacked_extension_path properly reads Chrome Preferences at .config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences and extracts all extension paths from extensions.settings.{id}.path
Metric function is_in_list correctly performs list membership check
Expected path '/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension' is semantically correct and matches the extraction location defined in setup config (line 23: unzip to /home/user/Desktop/)
Complete coverage: checking if extension path exists in Preferences verifies both extraction AND loading steps, since path only appears when extension is loaded via 'Load unpacked'
No postconfig needed: Chrome Preferences file is persistent and doesn't require reopening UI to read
Data flow is correct: setup extracts zip → user loads unpacked extension → Chrome writes to Preferences → getter reads Preferences → metric checks list membership
